ae-1rPJ.title: Google car: white pickup, often blurred
ae-1rPJ.summary: Newer Gen 4 coverage often uses a white pickup truck with a trekker camera, frequently blurred out. The front-cabin antenna sits in the middle here, but on the left in Qatar. Oman has a similar truck.

differs.how: Antenna at the front of the cabin is on the left, not the middle

ae-28Pr.title: Glitch: torn picture (rifts)
ae-28Pr.summary: Occasionally you may see rifts, glitches where the picture looks torn. They are much more common in Albania, Montenegro and Senegal.

differs.how: Rifts are far more common there
Rifts are far more common there
Rifts are far more common there

ae-43f2.title: Google car: black car, brake light visible
ae-43f2.summary: Some newer Gen 4 coverage uses a black car, and you can often see its brake light. Israel has a similar black Gen 4 car.

ae-9WlQ.title: Google car: white, side mirrors, sparse plants
ae-9WlQ.summary: A rare white Google car with visible side mirrors and sparse vegetation, found on one island.

ae-A3rG.title: Coverage: trekker amid sand dunes
ae-A3rG.summary: Remote trekker coverage surrounded by sand dunes in the far south, between the towns of Taraq and Alyhyali.

ae-AD1q.title: Curbs: striped black-white or black-yellow
ae-AD1q.summary: Almost all curbs are painted with stripes, either black and white or black and yellow.

ae-GHHD.title: Coverage: racetrack, east of capital
ae-GHHD.summary: Racetrack coverage slightly east of Abu Dhabi.

ae-HIpw.title: Road lines: yellow edges
ae-HIpw.summary: Yellow lines on the outside, and the middle line is white or yellow. Jordan, Israel and Oman use these too, so check other clues.

ae-Lxlq.title: Roads: many divided roads and roundabouts
ae-Lxlq.summary: Divided roads and roundabouts are both very common.

ae-M22T.title: Landscape: light-coloured mountains to the east
ae-M22T.summary: In the north, light-coloured mountains visible to the east point to the emirate of Ras al Khaimah.

ae-RONH.title: Pole: dark brown wood, three insulators on bar
ae-RONH.summary: Dark brown wooden poles with three insulators placed symmetrically along a horizontal metal bar. Oman has similar tops.

differs.how: Grey concrete poles with more widely spaced insulators

ae-SEgX.title: Landscape: mountains west, flat land east
ae-SEgX.summary: If mountains are to the west and the land is flat to the east, you are probably near the Gulf of Oman in the extreme east. Oman looks similar.

ae-YjWs.title: Skyline: many skyscrapers, a tall iconic tower
ae-YjWs.summary: A skyline packed with skyscrapers, including the famous Burj Khalifa.

ae-b44v.title: Sign: blue street names, narrow metal border
ae-b44v.summary: Blue street name signs with a thin metal border, specific to the biggest city.

ae-eQKo.title: Google car: sidewalk trekker
ae-eQKo.summary: In parts of the biggest city, including the old town, a Gen 4 trekker was carried on the sidewalk. You can sometimes see the operator's black hair.

ae-hV8q.title: Landscape: mountains only in the far east
ae-hV8q.summary: Mountains appear only in the far east of the country.

ae-jc6S.title: Google car: white with black roof rack
ae-jc6S.summary: In almost all older Gen 3 coverage (blurrier, softer colours), a white car with a visible black roof rack. It is the only white Google car in the Middle East.

ae-k0FZ.title: Coverage: trekkers at two forts and a zoo
ae-k0FZ.summary: In the inland city of Al Ain, trekker coverage far from the car coverage covers two forts and a zoo.

ae-lRZb.title: Sign: black-and-white striped signposts
ae-lRZb.summary: Many signposts have black-and-white stripes. In the Middle East, only Oman has these as well.

ae-lm-527.title: Google car: silver Gen 3 car
ae-lm-527.summary: If it feels like the Middle East and you see a silver Gen 3 car (older, blurrier camera), you can only be in the UAE.

ae-nA0w.title: Roads: unpaved residential streets
ae-nA0w.summary: Even though it is a rich country, residential roads are often unpaved.

ae-oJYL.title: Language: Arabic with English alongside
ae-oJYL.summary: Arabic script (lines and dots), and signs often carry English too because of heavy tourism. Qatar and Oman are similar, but English is uncommon on signs in Jordan.

differs.how: English is not common on Jordanian signs

ae-r48B.title: Coverage: mostly northeast corner only
ae-r48B.summary: Car coverage is mostly limited to the northeastern part of the country. The only car coverage elsewhere is on one island. All other remote coverage is trekker.

ae-z1O8.title: Houses: light stone, reddish sidewalks
ae-z1O8.summary: Houses in residential areas are typically light-coloured stone, and reddish stones are often used for the sidewalks.
